text: Welcome to SQL Dialects: T-SQL, PL/SQL, MySQL, and Beyond. You already know T-SQL deeply. This course is about something you may not have had reason to notice yet: T-SQL isn't just SQL. It's Microsoft's own dialect, built on a shared standard that no vendor ships unmodified.

Here's a plain select, from, where, filtering on order date. This exact query runs, with zero changes, on SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Snowflake. Basic querying is where the ANSI and ISO SQL standard is strongest, and where every dialect in this course agrees almost completely.

So where do they diverge, and why? Two of the three reasons are history and competition. Oracle's connect by, and SQL Server's cross apply, both solved a real problem with proprietary syntax, built from different design decisions made in the nineteen-eighties and nineties, long before today's standard existed in its current form.

The third reason is the big one: the SQL standard is deliberately incomplete. It has never fully standardized procedural extensions, things like stored procedures, control flow, and error handling. That's exactly why T-SQL and PL/SQL look so different from each other, and you'll spend a good chunk of this course living in that gap.

One more thing before we go further: this course teaches the SQL language, not database administration. You won't find backup and restore, security administration, or performance tuning internals here. Your T-SQL knowledge is the baseline every single lesson compares against.
Next lesson, we'll meet the players properly: SQL Server, Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, and the cloud warehouses that are reshaping this landscape again. See you there.
